subclass_note: Step 1.1 cited all ten facts [L1]-[L10] in one bracket while using two of them; step 4.1 made the inference "normal in the kernel and hence normal in G", which is invalid in general and is licensed here only by [L9] (cor-normal-sylow-subgroup-of-a-normal-subgroup-is-normal), which step 4.1 does not cite. The fact is declared and true of this situation, so the mathematics holds and the gap is inside the 30-second rule; but because step 1.1's shotgun bracket claimed every fact, the contract's input map recorded [L9] as used at a step that does not use it, and the coverage check passed without any step accounting for the actual inference. Recorded, not repaired: the step numbering and citation redistribution would move the item hash for a defect that is presentational, and step 8 is the wrong place to discover it.

prevention.ref: proof-contract could flag a single step whose input bracket names more than half the item's declared facts: a shotgun bracket satisfies the exactly-once input map while attributing every fact to one step.

subject: thm-jordan-holder-theorem-for-modules
subclass_note: Reader 2 rewrote this proof under R2-7 and the rewrite is correct — I re-derived the whole induction, including that the A != B branch's series of C has length n-2 and that the two factor multisets agree via A/C ~ M/B and B/C ~ M/A. But its closing sentence, "This also covers n=1, when C=0", is wrong about its own branch: at n=1 the module M is simple, so its only maximal proper submodule is 0 and A=B necessarily, making the A != B branch vacuous rather than covered. Taking the sentence at face value would put step 4.1's length count at n-2 = -1. The case is genuinely handled, by step 2.1's A = B branch.

prevention.ref: A reader that rewrites a proof owns its boundary sentences too; the rewrite was checked for validity but its inherited closing clause was not re-derived against the new argument.

subject: finite-smoke registers zero obligations across all 175 proof-bearing items in batches 1-3
subclass_note: finite-smoke.mjs reports "0 error(s), 0 check(s) over 0/26, 0/90, 0/59 item(s) carrying obligations" — it runs, exits zero and checks nothing, in three batches whose content is unusually rich in bounded finite claims: Sylow counts for groups of order at most fifteen, S_4, A_5 and Aff(Z/5); the length of Z/p^k; the reciprocity table for small odd primes; square-root counts modulo n; the order of Aut((Z/p)^2). These are exactly the claims a bounded countermodel search can falsify. The gate is green because nobody registered an obligation, which is indistinguishable in the output from a gate that searched and found nothing. CLOSED by Alpha contract-audit-3 (2026-08-17): the gate is live at 4 checks over 324 scoped items, and gate-liveness now reports "live finite-smoke 4 checks" instead of VACUOUS. Selected, each after reading the item and picking the registry check that probes ITS claim: binomial-congruence-solution-count on thm-unit-square-criterion-modulo-odd-prime-powers (exactly two solution classes; the search computes gcd(phi(p^k),2)=2 against actual counts), on lem-nonsingular-square-root-lift-modulo-odd-prime-powers (non-unique lifting would push the count above two at p^(k+1)), and on thm-unit-square-criterion-modulo-two-powers (reaches the modulus-2 and modulus-4 clauses only; 2^k for k>=3 has no primitive root and is outside the search by construction); cyclic-subgroup-lagrange on ex-length-of-z-modulo-p-to-the-k (the chain terms are the subgroups generated by p^i, whose orders the check computes). Three of this row's named candidates were declined on evidence rather than covered: the Sylow data table for orders at most fifteen (no registry check computes n_p = 1 mod p or n_p | m), the reciprocity table (no check computes Legendre symbols), and the order of Aut((Z/p)^2) (its step 4.1 states the argument "makes no matrix-group identification", so matrix-ring-laws-mod-n would test a route the proof deliberately avoids). Batch 3 and batches 4-7 carry no check: field theory, measure theory, topology and complex analysis match no registry entry, and the two poset checks are existence-of-failure witnesses for meets, whereas batch 7 asserts limit creation positively and its one failure item is a coequalizer in Set versus Grp. Detail and evidence: research/frontier-15-alpha-contract-audit.md.

prevention.ref: The tool-change half this row asked for already exists and is what caught the vacuity: gate-liveness.mjs distinguishes "searched, found nothing" from "no obligation registered" and reports VACUOUS with a nonzero exit, and the autopilot routes that vacuity to a contract-audit Alpha for check SELECTION (commit 1a63bc0b). What remained was the selection itself, which is judgement and is now done. finite-smoke.mjs also prints the coverage ratio (4/324) so the count can no longer be read as coverage.

subject: batches 1-2: 7 manifest rows disagreeing with the authored item frontmatter
subclass_note: Four batch-1 items declare a dependency the manifest lacks (prop-jacobi-symbol-on-units-is-a-homomorphism/thm-unit-criterion-modulo-n, thm-jacobi-map-kernel-and-square-subgroup/def-jacobi-symbol, cex-jacobi-symbol-one-does-not-imply-a-square/prop-unit-square-has-jacobi-symbol-one, ex-primes-dividing-x-squared-plus-three/thm-legendre-symbol-multiplicativity), left behind when reader 1 added the edges. In batch 2 the pair thm-lagrange + thm-number-of-bijections-of-a-finite-set sits on the manifest row for thm-groups-of-order-thirty-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup while the item that actually gained those inputs under R2-15 is thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup — a transcription slip that put the sync on the neighbouring theorem. Batch 3 had zero drift. All synced to the item frontmatter, which is the truth about what each proof cites.

prevention.ref: A manifest-vs-frontmatter diff belongs in the 6b gate set. Note for whoever writes it: compare YAML-parsed titles against JSON-parsed titles — comparing the raw frontmatter line against the parsed manifest value reports every backslash-bearing title as drift, which is how my first pass produced 30 false positives.

subject: 17 proof steps across the level name a check and perform none, and 4 contract boundary rows credit such a step as `checked`
subclass_note: The class is a numbered step whose entire content is an imperative naming work: "We treat the trivial $p$-subgroup and primes not dividing $|G|$." (thm-sylow-second-theorem 4.1), "We check the trivial quotient." (thm-fitting-subgroup-of-the-frattini-quotient 3.1), "We treat repeated terms and the zero module." (thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-artinian-modules 3.1), "Keep the two prime orderings and the order-twelve boundary case explicit." (thm-groups-of-order-p-squared-q-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup 4.1), "The preceding argument gives the conclusion under every hypothesis of the Statement." (4 items, contentless filler), "We check fields of characteristic two.", "We check the initial term $\mathbb Z$.", "We check the inverse map and the zero ring.", "Remove zero or repeated summands and include the zero-generated case.", "We apply orbit-stabiliser, including the unique/trivial Sylow case.", "The forward implication is published." (a repository status claim standing in for a step). Two items — prop-endomorphisms-form-a-ring and thm-endomorphism-ring-of-a-finite-direct-sum-as-hom-matrices — had NO proof at all: every numbered step was an announcement, one of them naming four ring axioms it never verified. Why this is a boundary defect and not only a prose defect: thm-sylow-second-theorem's contract marked `zero` and `degenerate` as `checked` with the evidence "is resolved in step 4.1", quoting the announcement verbatim. boundary-audit could not see it, because its `checked` detector only tests whether the credited step NUMBER exists in the proof, and 4.1 does exist. All 17 repaired: the real discharge written for each named case, and full proofs authored for the two items that had none. Each repaired item re-precheck'd, its contract entry regenerated, and proof-contract --strict re-run to 0 errors.

prevention.ref: Two tool changes, both live. (1) tools/announcement-steps.mjs, new: flags a numbered step whose every sentence opens by naming an activity and none of which states an outcome, splitting hits into `strong` and `weak` so a terse but real discharge is not swept up. Its verb list is grown from live misses, never guessed — the first version missed 2 of 3 known instances because inline math inside a NAMED case counted as work, and a later one missed "Keep the two prime orderings..." because `Keep` was absent. Cross-check it with an orthogonal scan (steps with no math, no relation symbol, under 170 chars) before trusting a zero result; that scan is noisy but it is what surfaced 3 further verbs. (2) tools/boundary-audit.mjs gains a fourth contradiction signal: a `checked` row crediting a step that IS an announcement, which is airtight because both halves are mechanical. Verified against a purpose-built fixture — it fires on the announcement-credited row and stays silent on the row crediting real work. NOT done, and deliberately: stripping the item's own title from the template-cluster key collapses frontier-15's interpolated rows into 31 clusters, but most are honest ('this item states no biconditional' is the true disposition for 45 items and has one natural phrasing), so it would make a precision-first gate noisy.

subject: thm-sylow-third-theorem chooses a Sylow subgroup with no dependency establishing that one exists, and declares a fact no step uses
subclass_note: Found by the independent DeepSeek refuter and confirmed from disk. Step 1.1 read "Let a Sylow subgroup $P$ act by conjugation on the Sylow set", which presupposes Syl_p(G) is nonempty — that is Sylow I, and thm-sylow-first-theorem appeared nowhere in `deps`. The item's own [L4] even says existence "is proved later". None of the five declared dependencies supplies it. Separately lem-product-with-normal-subgroup was declared as [L5] and used by no step. Both were invisible to proof-contract because step 1.1 carried a BLANKET citation of all five facts, which satisfies the every-fact-is-used check while telling the input map nothing true. Repaired: thm-sylow-first-theorem added to deps and to the facts block, step 1.1 rewritten to draw P from a set a cited fact has made nonempty, the unused fact removed, and steps 2.1 and 3.1 — which cited nothing at all while using Sylow II, the fixed-point congruence and the normalizer-index formula — written out with honest citations. The mathematics was correct throughout; only the dependency trace was false.

prevention.ref: The enabling pattern is the blanket citation: a first step listing every fact in the item, which makes `citation-uses` and `step-entry-input-omitted` vacuously satisfied for facts no step actually uses. Seen on at least 8 batch-2 items (thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-... cites 12 at step 1.1, cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five cites 15, ex-heisenberg-... cites 12). A proof-contract check worth writing: flag a step whose input list names more than N facts AND is the only step naming most of them; the honest cases are rare and can be upheld on the record like a boundary row.

subject: thm-sylow-second-theorem's title stated Sylow II with no finiteness marker
subclass_note: Reported as FATAL by the independent DeepSeek refuter, which supplied a correct counterexample: in the infinite dihedral group the maximal 2-subgroups <r^n s> split into two conjugacy classes by the parity of n, since conjugation sends r^n s to r^(n+2k) s or r^(2j-n) s. I verified that computation and it is right for the general notion of Sylow subgroup. I adjudicate it NONFATAL rather than fatal, on two pieces of evidence the refuter did not have: this library's def-sylow-p-subgroup is stated only for finite G, so the title's phrase cannot be read outside finite groups in-library; and a self-tested scan of the level found six other titles using the same convention (cor-sylow-subgroup-normal-iff-unique, thm-normalizer-of-a-sylow-normalizer, thm-frattini-argument, cor-frattini-subgroup-is-contained-in-the-fitting-subgroup, ex-a-four-is-not-nilpotent, cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences). It was underspecified, not false in the library's own vocabulary. Title still amended to "in a finite group" as step-6 polish, because Sylow I and Sylow III both carry the marker and the title should stand alone in the index and flowchart, where the reader has not opened the definition.

prevention.ref: The scan that produced the six-item convention finding was itself broken on first run and returned zero hits — its `titleFinite` regex matched the very title it was meant to flag, so the empty result was meaningless. It only became evidence after a self-test asserting that the known-bad title flags and the repaired one clears. Any title/statement hypothesis-drift scan should carry that self-test inline; a zero-hit scan with no positive control is not a finding.

subject: risk-report reported 125 items unreviewed while 33 of them carried complete Alpha reviews under the wrong key
subclass_note: risk-report --require-reviewed demands risk_review.notes; Alpha-a had written its dispositions under risk_review.disposition. The 33 rows were substantive, per-item and in several cases recorded confirmed-fatal repairs with their own ledger rows — they were not missing work, they were a field-name mismatch, and the gate could not tell the two apart. I read all 33 before touching them and renamed the key; no rationale was written, weakened or invented to clear the gate. The remaining 92 were genuinely unreviewed and were read and reviewed individually. Recorded because the failure mode is worth naming: a gate that reports 'missing' cannot distinguish absent work from misfiled work, and the honest response to a large missing-count is to read the artifacts before assuming the work was never done.

prevention.ref: risk-report could distinguish the two cases cheaply: if contracts[id].risk_review exists but lacks `notes`, emit a distinct code (risk-review-malformed) naming the keys it did find, instead of the same risk-review-missing it emits for an absent block. The remedy line for the two is different — one is 'do the review', the other is 'rename the key' — and conflating them cost a full re-read of 33 completed reviews.

subject: 518 boundary rows across 88 batch-2 items are generated from the item's title and statement rather than written as dispositions
subclass_note: 26 items have a worksheet that is generated end to end and 62 are partly generated; batches 1 and 3-7 have none, so this is one Beta's habit and not a level-wide convention. The shape is "<title>: <stock clause for this axis> for \u201c<statement>\u201d", with `not_applicable` reasons drawn from a fixed set of seven phrasings ('has no set, family, sum, product, or series allowed to be empty', 'is a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional', ...) and `checked` evidence reading 'is resolved in step X.Y: "<verbatim step text>"'. boundary-audit's template detector reports NO cluster over these 518 rows, because interpolating each item's own title and statement makes every row textually unique — the normalizer strips the id and quoted spans but not the title. The independent DeepSeek refuter hit the same class from the other side on fs-finite-nilpotent-and-solvable-groups-coincide, whose iff-forward and iff-reverse rows call the claim 'a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional' when 'finite nilpotent and finite solvable groups are the same' is plainly an equivalence; I confirmed that from disk. NOT repaired at scale: rewriting 518 rows as real dispositions is the owning Beta's work with its sources to hand, and a bulk rewrite by me would reproduce the original defect in a new hand. The four rows that credited an announcement step ARE repaired, via f15-a-rr-001. STEP-9 SWEEP, STILL OPEN. Its recorded closing condition is a rewrite of the batch-2 boundary worksheets by the owning Beta, and no Beta runs at step 9, so the condition is not met and the row stays open deliberately. What step 9 DID establish, so the owner is not reading a bare 'unfinished': (a) the measurement in this row's prevention field was implemented — 454 of batch 2's 720 boundary rows match a stock tail or the 'is resolved in step X.Y:' frame under a conservative detector, 7 items fully generated and 81 partly; (b) boundary-audit still reports 0 template clusters and 0 contradicted over those 720 rows, confirming the interpolated title defeats its normalizer; (c) an independent targeted detector was run across ALL SEVEN batches for the one sub-class whose falsity is airtight — a not_applicable iff row on an item whose Statement carries two directions — returning 18 candidates, 16 over-fires and 2 real, both in batch 2, both now repaired (f15-S9-006); (d) NEITHER of the two concealed a mathematical defect: each item's own proof discharges exactly the obligation its row denied existed. So the residue is contract quality, not a hidden fatal defect, on the evidence available at step 9. What remains is the ~450 generated rows themselves, and rewriting them at scale is still the owning Beta's work with its sources to hand. OWNER ACCEPTANCE (2026-08-17, in-session): publish without the batch-2 worksheet rework — the mathematics and dependencies are cleared (86/86 fatals repaired, 398/398 current judge pairs, closure with no allowances); the targeted detector found 2 real false rows in 18 candidates and neither concealed a mathematical defect. The rework remains available to any future cycle via the recorded task file.

prevention.ref: The measurement is a 30-line script: count rows whose reason matches one of the seven stock tails or the 'is resolved in step X.Y:' frame, then group by item. Items at 8/8 are the ones to route back. Making boundary-audit itself fail on this needs care — stripping the title from the cluster key does collapse the rows, but it also collapses 45 honest 'this item states no biconditional' rows, and this tool's stated design is precision over recall because a detector firing on a third of the corpus trains readers to skim it.

subject: cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five [L11] stops mid-clause at "and the resulting map.", so the biconditional it states has no right-hand conclusion and licenses nothing
subclass_note: The cited thm-internal-external-semidirect-product-equivalence states that N normal, G=NH, N cap H = 1 hold iff conjugation restricts to an action alpha and the resulting map Phi : N rtimes_alpha H -> G, (n,h) |-> nh IS AN ISOMORPHISM carrying the canonical factors onto N and H. The Facts line reproduced the antecedent and the first conjunct of the consequent and then ended with the words 'and the resulting map.' — no predicate. Step 3.1 concludes 'the internal product is G iso C_5 x H' and cites [L11] for it, so the step's stated support asserts nothing about the map at all. The mathematics of the item is correct: with N_5 normal, G = N_5 H, N_5 cap H = 1 and the conjugation action trivial (step 2.1, since gcd(21,4)=1), L11+L12 do give G iso C_5 x H. What was wrong is the citation, and only the citation. Not caught by citation-fidelity.mjs: the contract's recorded quote for L11 is the cited item's full statement section (itself cut at the tool's 400-char cap) and it does appear in the cited item, so --fail-on-missing-quote passes. Not caught by truncated-citation.mjs either: that detector compares a fact line against the cited section as a PREFIX and flags short prefixes, and this line is not a prefix — it paraphrases the antecedent before truncating, so the ratio heuristic never fires. The gap is that no gate compares the ITEM's fact line against the CONTRACT's recorded quote; both are checked against the cited item and neither against each other.

prevention.ref: A detector comparing each item's [F#]/[L#] line against its own contract row's `quote` would catch this class directly, and it is the one comparison the existing pair of tools does not make: citation-fidelity checks quote-vs-cited-item, truncated-citation checks factline-vs-cited-item, neither checks factline-vs-quote. A cheap first cut: flag any fact line ending in a determiner or bare noun phrase ('the resulting map.', 'the following holds.') before its citation parenthesis.

subject: thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup [L4] appends "le H" to the kernel equation, which thm-left-coset-action-and-its-kernel does not state
subclass_note: The published statement is ker rho = Core_G(H), full stop. The fact line printed ker rho = Core_G(H) le H, and step 3.1 uses exactly that extra clause twice — 'has kernel K subseteq H' and 'K le H gives 3 = [G:H] | [G:K]'. So the inflation is load-bearing, not decorative. It is nonfatal rather than fatal because Core_G(H) le H is immediate from def-core-of-a-subgroup (the intersection of all conjugates includes the g=1 term) and is stated outright by the published lem-core-is-largest-normal-subgroup-contained, which sits on group-actions-and-cayleys-theorem — a page this one already requires. Repaired by restoring [L4] to the source statement and adding [L13] citing lem-core-is-largest-normal-subgroup-contained for K le H, with that id added to deps and step 3.1's input list. The contract entry was regenerated, and its L4 quote had been correct all along, which is the second time in this run that the contract was faithful and the item was not.

prevention.ref: Same missing comparison as f15-6c-001: fact line versus its own contract quote. Here the contract quote is verbatim-correct and the item's line has one extra relational atom appended inside the same display, so a diff of the two would have printed it as a one-token addition.

published source, Statement — prints no inclusion

subject: thm-one-step-simultaneous-root-extension [L4] reads "is finite, and therefore algebraic" while thm-finitely-generated-algebraic-extensions-are-finite states only finiteness
subclass_note: The 'therefore algebraic' half is what step 4.1 actually needs — the whole point of that step is to conclude L/F is algebraic — so the inflation is load-bearing. The bridging fact, every finite field extension is algebraic, is published as thm-finite-field-extensions-are-algebraic on algebraic-extensions-degree-and-finite-fields, which this page's requires closure already reaches and which a sibling item on the same page (cor-finite-extension-of-a-perfect-field-is-simple) already cites correctly. Repaired by restoring [L4] to the source statement verbatim, adding [L6] for the bridging theorem, adding it to deps, and splitting step 4.1's reasoning across the two facts.

prevention.ref: A fact line joining two claims with 'and therefore' or 'hence' while naming a single source is a mechanically detectable shape; when the trailing claim is not a substring-equivalent of anything in the cited statement, it needs its own citation. This is the same factline-versus-quote diff as f15-6c-001 and f15-6c-002.

subject: thm-monads-on-a-preorder-are-exactly-closure-operators [L1] attributes the natural-transformation criterion Fp le Gp to prop-preorders-as-categories-and-monotone-maps-as-functors, which states only that functors between preorders are monotone maps
subclass_note: The added clause is the entire mechanism of the theorem: steps 1.1 and 1.2 read eta as the family p le Tp and mu as T(Tp) le Tp, and both cite [L1] for the right to do so. The cited proposition does say 'a preorder determines a category with at most one morphism between any two objects', and the criterion follows from that in two lines — a morphism Fp -> Gp exists exactly when Fp le Gp, and naturality squares commute for want of a second arrow — so it is nonfatal. Repaired by restoring [L1] to the source statement, which includes the at-most-one-morphism clause, and deriving the natural-transformation criterion inline in step 1.1, where the derivation is now visible instead of hidden in a citation. Step 1.2 already used the at-most-one-arrow clause explicitly for the monad diagrams, so the item was half-honest about its route already.

prevention.ref: citation-faithfulness-screen.mjs did flag this line as a candidate (L1 -> prop-preorders-as-categories-and-monotone-maps-as-functors: Rightarrow, leq — two operators the cited statement never mentions), and it was among the 42 candidates the run's earlier stages left unread. The detector worked; the routing did not. The cheap change is to require a written disposition per candidate at 6b, the way risk-report requires a risk_review, rather than printing candidates for an optional read.

subject: ex-the-ultrafilter-monad-on-a-finite-set [L3] restates thm-ultrafilter-lemma without its "Assume the Axiom of Choice" hypothesis
subclass_note: The published thm-ultrafilter-lemma opens 'Assume the Axiom of Choice' and its own remarks account for exactly where that is spent (Zorn at step 4.1). The fact line printed 'Every proper filter is contained in an ultrafilter' flat, then wrote 'assuming this principle' for the second half — so the choice cost was attached to the consequence rather than to the theorem that incurs it, and a reader could take clause 1 for a ZF theorem. Nonfatal because step 4.1 does say 'Assuming [L3]', so nothing downstream claims a choice-free result. Repaired by printing the hypothesis on the theorem where the source prints it, and by matching the source's 'every filter' rather than 'every proper filter' (def-filter in this library already excludes the empty set, so the two agree, but the source's wording is the one to reproduce). This matters more than usual on this page because the batch-4 and batch-7 items around it keep explicit choice ledgers.

prevention.ref: A cited item whose statement section opens with a bolded 'Assume the Axiom of Choice' / 'Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice' and whose citing fact line contains no choice word is a two-line grep, and the corpus already marks those hypotheses in a fixed bolded form. Batch 4 gets this right in five places (thm-countable-union-of-countable, thm-countable-subsets-of-omega-one-are-bounded, thm-well-ordering-theorem, thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor, thm-zorn), which is what makes the one miss detectable as a miss rather than a convention.

subject: cex-connected-domain-need-not-be-star-shaped [L1] cites lem-punctured-rn-is-polygonally-connected for an arbitrary puncture R^n minus {p}, while the published lemma states only R^n minus {0}
subclass_note: Generalising the puncture from the origin to an arbitrary point is true but needs translation-invariance of polygonal connectedness, which the cited lemma does not supply and no other declared dependency states. It is not load-bearing here: the counterexample is U = C minus {0}, so the p = 0 instance is the only one used, and step 1.1 invokes [L1] on exactly that set. Repaired by restating [L1] as the source states it. Recorded rather than waved through because the same inflated line copied onto a page that punctures somewhere other than the origin would be a real gap, and the item text is what gets copied.

prevention.ref: Same factline-versus-quote diff as f15-6c-001 through 003; here the difference is a single substituted symbol inside a set-builder, which a token-level diff of the two strings surfaces immediately.

subject: cor-algebraic-closures-are-isomorphic-over-the-base
subclass_note: The title read 'Assuming Choice, any two algebraic closures are base-isomorphic, generally nonuniquely' and the Statement repeated the claim as 'Such an isomorphism generally need not be unique.' Step 3.1 of the same item says the opposite about its own scope: 'The argument proves existence only and makes no uniqueness assertion.' Nonuniqueness is therefore asserted in the reader-facing title and Statement of a landmark item and established nowhere in it. Repaired by narrowing (owner repair 3): the title now stops at 'base-isomorphic' and the Statement says 'No uniqueness of the isomorphism is asserted.' The claim is not lost to the library -- fs-algebraic-closure-is-unique-up-to-unique-isomorphism, on the same pair, actually proves nonuniqueness by exhibiting the nonidentity Q-automorphism of an algebraic closure of Q carrying a root of x^2+1 to its negative, and its own [L4] already restates this corollary as existence only. The narrowed Statement and that consumer's citation now agree exactly.

prevention.ref: the phrase was in the step-1 scaffold title verbatim; a title asserting a second claim ('generally nonuniquely', 'and not conversely', 'necessarily') is checkable at step 3 against the strategy, before any proof exists

subject: thm-separable-closures-exist-and-are-isomorphic-over-the-base
subclass_note: The Statement read 'Any two separable closures are F-isomorphic, generally nonuniquely', while step 2.2 ends 'The construction does not assert uniqueness.' The proof builds one F-embedding and shows it is onto; it neither proves nor exhibits nonuniqueness. Unlike the algebraic-closure case the scaffold title was clean, so the clause was added at authoring. Repaired by narrowing: the Statement now ends 'Any two separable closures are F-isomorphic. No uniqueness of the isomorphism is asserted.'

prevention.ref: same shape as frontier-15-S8-01 on the same page; when one item in a pair acquires an unproved 'generally nonuniquely' the sibling should be checked in the same pass

subject: thm-extension-generated-by-separable-elements-is-separable
subclass_note: Step 1.2 built the tower F <= F(s_1) <= ... <= F(s_1,...,s_r), showed only that each s_j has separable minimal polynomial over the preceding field, and then applied [L1] (thm-separability-is-transitive) to conclude the whole subextension is separable over F. Transitivity requires each adjacent extension to be separable elementwise; 'the generator is separable' gives that only via the one-generator case of the very theorem being proved, so the inference was circular. Both lanes found it independently and stated it precisely. (2) 'Substituting the group-word identities into the same multiplication law turns them into associativity, the unit laws and the inverse laws' compresses four instantiations of a T(a) = a mu_A, one of which is materially different: for W = [[x],[x^{-1}]] the two entries are both POSITIVE letters of the alphabet TA, so W is reduced and T(a)(W) is the honest two-letter word, while mu_A multiplies them inside F(A) where they cancel to the empty word. That asymmetry is where the identity comes from and the text does not flag it. Used correctly, not assumed. NOT repaired: step 8 is fatal-only under R1, and this is exposition rather than a gap.

The old step 1.3 asserted the restriction-of-scalars determinant identity. The repair proves transitivity from restriction fibres, embedding formulas, and multiplicativity of separable and inseparable degrees.

The old maximal-subgroup argument falsely made G/H simple. The repair separates each nonidentity automorphism by a character obtained from the invariant-factor decomposition, then applies cyclic Kummer theory to its fixed field.

subclass_note: tools/reflow.mts documents that 'each numbered step must sit on one physical line' and joins a step's soft-wrapped continuation lines into one line. precheck.mts credits a step only when its line ENDS with a bracketed justification tag from PROP_TAG. [L2, L3, step 1.1]') and the step continues on following lines, so whole-batch precheck passed (15201 items, 0 failing on the pre-5a tree). Running the canonical reflow tool on five such items merged each step into one line whose trailing bracket was a content tag ('[finite counting]', '[finite-dimensional duality, square-sum Holder]') or no tag at all, producing bad-tag/untagged-steps failures on items that had passed. Local remedy used here: re-split each step line immediately after its first bracketed tag, restoring the passing convention for the five edited items. The tool and the checker disagree about the canonical step shape; one of them needs the owner's decision (fix reflow to split after the first tag, or extend PROP_TAG to the corpus's content tags). RESOLVED at 5b-cross (phase-2-next-18, 2026-09-14): tools/reflow.mts now keeps a numbered step's line when it already ends with a bracketed group, instead of joining its continuation into it, so the tag the line-based checker reads stays at the end of the step's physical line. The alternative remedy (extending PROP_TAG in the app repo) remains open and does not conflict with this fix.

subject: def-logarithmic-potential-and-energy
finding: The remark says energy is defined when “at least one” of the positive and negative kernel integrals is finite, with value in (-infinity,+infinity]. Let rho_n be normalized arclength on the circle of radius 1/4 centered at e^n, and let sigma be the probability mixture with weights proportional to 1/n^2. Distinct circles are more than distance 1 apart, so the positive-part integral is only the same-circle contribution and is finite (each same-circle integral is log 4, weighted by a summable multiple of 1/n^4). For n<m, cross-circle distances are at least e^m/2, so the negative-part integral is bounded below by a positive multiple of sum_m (m-log 2)/m^2 times sum_{n<m}1/n^2, which diverges. Thus one part is finite, as the stated criterion allows, but the energy is -infinity, outside the claimed range.

Current independent review: Read Proof 1.1-4.1, all seven facts and actual connectivity, cubical disk, pair exactness, relative basis and finite cellular-approximation suppliers. The removed original core, retained ambient boundary and total inserted-piece dimension were misdescribed. An arbitrary p=0 framed two-point attachment need not give an oriented trace. Current definition requires both attaching components to match one handle orientation. Raw upper-handle core and cylinder retractions did not glue to the asserted face-relative retraction. Its sufficiently small closed product tube lies in the interior of the inserted piece; the entire large disk factor need not be an interior tube. Degree-zero group quotients, an always infinite cyclic kernel, and unsupplied CW prerequisites were invalid. Model transport and homotopies of attaching maps give the CW pairs, with cellular replacement understood as in the single-cell lemma. The q-cell preserves components and pi_i through q-2; q>=p+2 gives the isomorphism at i=p. Supplied basepoint paths specify comparisons; p=1 works with nonabelian normal kernel, p=0 is excluded. The incoming connector kills z; simple connectivity gives cyclic image, possibly finite, not necessarily infinite.

Only positive-degree w_i vanish (w0=1); vanishing is not sufficiency. AC is declared for the characteristic-class conclusions.

subject: thm-borel-and-maximal-torus-conjugacy-over-algebraically-closed-field

evidence.note: A largest-dimensional smooth connected solvable subgroup exists by bounded integer dimensions and is Borel. Its complete quotient admits a fixed point for every other Borel; the explicitly justified nonempty finite-type fibre has a rational lift, and schematic density upgrades point inclusion to Bprime subset conjugate B. Borel maximality gives equality, so all Borels have maximum dimension and complete quotients. Every maximal torus is contained in a Borel by maximizing solvable dimension among overgroups; after Borel conjugation, maximality in G implies maximality in B, allowing the solvable torus theorem. Extending the nonzero cotangent class to a finite basis and Nakayama gives a parameter; the exact published quotient lemma gives regularity and dimension d-1 under AC. The published Krull proof has a nonfatal forward-reference defect, separately routed as reader:26:1; its later determinant-trick argument establishes the required separatedness. Source: Wlodarczyk §2.1 p.3; direct definitions and quoted supplier statements checked.

Accepted the boundary convention that each member has disjoint components and distinct members repeat no component, as required for counting boundary members. Wlodarczyk Definition 2.1.1 p.3 expressly has disjoint components; Stacks 0BIA complete proof gives the parameter-product and regular-intersection equivalence. At any point each boundary member supplies at most one distinct parameter. Empty union has unit equation, and a subfamily remains a subset of the same parameters. The older manifest lacked this algorithm qualification; current SNC definition itself is preserved.

Accepted correction of the counterexample: for a nontrivial finite separable extension the induced completion map K→L fails to be an isomorphism, regardless of abstract field isomorphisms. Flatness and the zero-dimensional regular fibre give mB=n. Flat tensoring identifies each graded piece with its residue extension; finite-dimensional scalar extension detects both ideal-containment directions, including N=0 and I=0. Equal residue fields give finite quotient isomorphisms by induction and hence the inverse-limit isomorphism, using the completion definition only. No additional choice is needed. Source Wlodarczyk Lemma 2.4.1 p.5 is interpreted with its equal-residue restriction.

Accepted clarification of the algebraically closed core versus broader explicit fields and inherited AC, and replacement of definition-only regular/smooth equivalence by the precise perfect-field criterion. Characteristic-zero fields are perfect; the geometric regularity field test and standard-smooth theorem apply to finite-type algebras. Integral separated finite-type variety and reduced final-theorem conventions are kept distinct. Nonclosed-field descent and perfect-field positive-characteristic derivative uses are expressly qualified. Source Wlodarczyk §2 opening p.3 and exact published geometric-regularity statements checked.

Accepted positive-mark and componentwise generic-nonvanishing prerequisites for canonical resolution. A globally nonzero ideal may vanish on another disjoint smooth component, so global I≠0 cannot replace generic nonzero on each component; mark 0 has full support. The definition continues to allow those formal marked ideals but does not assert support-clearing existence for them. Support and ordered boundary match Wlodarczyk Definitions 2.1.1–2.1.3 p.3 and the current order/SNC/conventions suppliers.

Accepted the intrinsic ideal generated by I and local derivations, with explicit AC inherited from finite locally free smooth differentials. Universality identifies derivations with the dual basis to a basis of exact differentials; Leibniz gives the finite generator list and coherence over the Noetherian smooth scheme. This repairs confusion between relative coordinate rank and local-ring dimension at a nonclosed point. D^0=I and the mark-zero last derivative are defined; in characteristic p, D(x^p)=(x^p). Source §2.6 p.6 and direct differential/derivation supplier interfaces checked.

Accepted the correction of extension to insertion of isomorphisms retaining exactly the original nontrivial blowups, as Wlodarczyk Definition 2.1.5 p.4 specifies. Exceptional ideal inverse powers have the correct sign, isomorphisms have empty exceptional divisor and unit ideal, and the ordered old boundary precedes the new divisor. Actual ideal containment is supplied next by the controlled-transform lemma, rather than presumed for arbitrary centers. The broader earlier extension could insert new blowups and would not express smooth-functorial sequence comparisons.

Accepted replacement of the unsupported coefficient selection by the free normal graded module. At x in regular C, R/P is a domain and gr_P R=(R/P)[U]; a nonzero initial class of degree j<μ survives localization at the component generic point P. That point belongs to the support, contradicting its order j. Pullback then gives I(D)^μ divisibility; changing a principal generator or exceptional equation multiplies the controlled section by a unit. Empty C and μ=0 give trivial containment. Exact parameter-generation, regular-sequence and invertible-center suppliers hold under AC. The published normal-graded proof was read completely; its erroneous Remark locator is separately recorded under reader:26:2. Source Lemma 2.2.1 p.4 checked independently.

Accepted the essential perfection qualification and formal/algebraic derivative comparison; amended the malformed duplicated Proof heading only. Read every step and exact coefficient-field, completed-power-series and smooth-differential suppliers. Leibniz lowers order by at most i over all fields. Over a perfect field separating residue coordinates give a K-compatible coefficient field and parameter expansion; finite Taylor/Hasse coefficients of degree <μ cut out the order locus without factorial division. In characteristic zero or p>μ, a selected nonzero homogeneous coefficient survives differentiation, proving both support directions and D^μ(I)=O iff all orders ≤μ. For K=Fp(a), x^p-a has order 1 yet all K-derivatives vanish, so the older unqualified converse is false. The j=0, i=0 and zero-stalk cases are respected. Source §2.6 pp.6–7. Heading correction is mechanical and has no separate defect row.

Accepted the actual smooth-composition relative-dimension supplier replacing the étale-only citation. Transitivity and Ω_B/A=0 give a surjection of finite locally free differential modules; the correct composition theorem gives equal ranks, hence an isomorphism. Dualization extends every base derivation and writes all target derivations as their B-linear combinations. Leibniz proves both ideal inclusions, then iteration includes i=0. The argument works in every characteristic and does not need a residue-field equality. Exact smooth-differential, formal-étale and relative-dimension supplier statements read; source Lemma 2.6.5 p.7.

Contract enrichment was sound, but current step 1.1 applied σ:K→K′ to the general ring element cD((φ*)^-1g). This is ill-typed unless that section happens to be constant. Replaced σ by the section-ring isomorphism φ*; semilinearity then gives φ*(cD(h))=σ(c)φ*(D(h)). Conjugation proves additivity, Leibniz and K′-linearity with inverse transport, and exactly identifies derivative generators; iteration includes i=0. Statement and dependency interfaces unchanged. Exact morphism/derivation definitions checked; source Lemma 4.3.1. This is a complete surgical proof repair, with no consumer statement change.

Accepted removal of boundary members containing a component of S and the direct blowup-chart restriction proof. Such members restrict to the zero equation, not a Cartier divisor, so the older unrestricted boundary was invalid. At x in S maximal ideals quotient, giving support inclusion. For a smooth nested center the parameter-generation theorem adapts x defining S and y defining C within S. Charts indexed by x have empty strict S; charts indexed by y identify S′ with Bl_C S and exceptional division commutes with restriction. Induction proves the stated test-sequence identity; components lost entirely yield no stalks. Source Lemma 2.10.3 pp.14–15 and exact parameter/chart suppliers checked. No power-series lifting is assumed.

Accepted the previously missing total order on Sub(E): increasing labels padded by 0 are compared lexicographically with 0 below all labels, as source §3 p.16 prescribes. Empty subset has zero sequence and finite E gives finitely many rho-values. The resolution definition states regular maximum centers and lexicographic decrease of inv or nu; no claim that finite-support rational lexicographic sequences alone are well founded is made. Étale pullbacks carry boundary labels by the given order. All current marked-ideal, equivalence, sequence and SNC interfaces checked.

Accepted μ≥1 for T=D^(μ-1), and perfection/p>μ qualifications in the derivative characterization. Mark 0 remains possible for maximal order but has no negative-index tangent ideal. An order-one section of T gives a regular hypersurface; repeated Leibniz gives T⊂m at every support point, so V(u) contains the local support. Transversality is only asserted when the tangent class extends with boundary classes to parameters. Exact earlier derivative support and regular-quotient suppliers checked; source Definitions 2.7.1/2.7.5 pp.7–8.

Accepted the inclusion title and replacement of the old derivative-ideal calculation by a direct generator computation. In a normal-coordinate blowup chart δ=yσ*D is regular and δ(y)/y is regular. For σ*f=y^μg, y^(1-μ)σ*(Df)=δg+μ(δy/y)g, and the undifferentiated generator becomes yg. Thus the first-derivative inclusion has the correct direction; monotonicity and center-support inheritance induct up to r=μ, including r=0 equality and marking-zero endpoint. No factorial or characteristic division is used. Full source Lemma 2.6.3 pp.6–7 checked; the old source-style intermediate assertion was not relied upon.

Flat blowup base change identifies the pulled-back blowup, which is an isomorphism for an empty center. Flatness commutes with saturation (kernel to localization, then filtered union), justifying strict-boundary pullbacks in F5. Source Proposition 2.4.2 p.5 and exact flat-base-change/universal-property statements checked.

Accepted perfection/p>μ restriction for the restriction-support assertion while retaining all-characteristic equivalence. Marks μ-i for i=0,…,μ-1 are positive, their product is μ!, and the explicit exponents μ!/(μ-i) match the marked sum. μ=1 gives C(I,1)=(I,1). Source Definition 2.10.1 pp.13–14 has a printed index shorthand corrected by its own Lemma 2.10.2 proof.

Accepted the complete residual-max and local-neighbourhood correction, and deletion of false general companion equivalence. On Noetherian smooth components generic nonzero implies all stalks nonzero; closed order-superlevels stabilize with empty intersection, so residual order is bounded. Empty support and r=0 route separately. Removing {ord N>r} gives maximal order on a neighbourhood of the support; positive marks r and μ-r justify the sum. Exact order additivity in the regular graded domain gives companion support=support(I,μ)∩{ord N=r}. The disjoint-plane example I=(x²) and (u,v)², μ=2 disproves the old equivalence by unequal supports. Resolving the companion targets maximal residual order; it is not asserted to resolve the entire original support at once. Source Definition 3.0.10 p.20 and earlier order/sum suppliers checked.

Accepted perfection and p>μ for the derivative-homogenization containment. Finite sum runs i=0,…,μ-1, uses ordinary ideal products, and μ≥1 makes tangent ideal defined. μ=1 gives H=I; T(H)=T(I) is an algebraic Leibniz consequence proved by the properties lemma. The derivative comparison requires μ>1, so no homogenization with undefined marking -1 is used. The equivalence assertion retains its separate authored proof and does not require the derivative converse. Source §2.9 pp.9–10 and current tangent/sum definitions checked.

Accepted localisation of the unit-transform conclusion to a neighbourhood of the chosen support component. In the UFD R, the height-one prime is (u); DVR localization gives I_P=(u^μ), and prime cancellation gives I=(u^μ)J. Maximal order forces ord(u)=1 and J=R at every x in C, so C is regular and isolated from other support components. Its Cartier blowup is an isomorphism whose controlled ideal becomes unit near C; other distant support components can remain. The existence of a codimension-one support component rules out μ=0 (whose support is all X). Exact UFD, DVR and regular quotient supplier hypotheses hold under AC; source Step 1a p.16.

Accepted correction of the reversed support inclusion. The inductive smaller transformed derivative ideal has the larger order-superlevel support, so C_i⊂supp(I_i,μ)⊂supp(D^j I_i,μ-j)⊂supp([D^jI]_i,μ-j). This makes every next transform defined; monotonicity and the one-step inclusion prove [D^jI]_(i+1)⊂D^j(I_(i+1)). j=0 gives equality, j=μ has marking zero and full support, and identity steps are harmless. Source Lemma 2.6.4 p.7 and the two preceding authored transform suppliers checked.

Accepted perfection/p>μ carried into the maximal-order derivative theorem. D^(μ-i)(D^i I)=D^μ I=O; the earlier safe-characteristic criterion proves maximal order at positive residual mark. At i=μ the ideal is O and mark is 0, so maximal order follows directly. i=0 is the original hypothesis. The exact criterion and recursive derivative interface checked; source §2.7.

The unchanged mathematical argument and contract enrichment are sound. Fixed the Given paragraph citing F4 for associated graded, which is actually F3 (F4 is the product transform identity). gr_m domain gives exact positive power order, including zero and unit ideals; scaling by k≥1 preserves both support directions even for μ=0. Controlled division scales y^-μ to its kth power, so induction gives precisely the same test sequences and every transformed support under the same boundary. Accepted the direct normal-form and arbitrary-prime Hasse bound rather than an unsafe ordinary-derivative proof. I⊂J^μ plus order μ at c gives a nonzero degree-μ transverse initial form over κ(c); its dehomogenization stays a nonzero polynomial of degree ≤μ on every exceptional chart. For a top-degree monomial, its Hasse derivative is a nonzero constant; Hasse-Leibniz sends m^(d+1) into m, so polynomial order ≤degree at every fibre prime. Quotient restriction only raises order, giving the same bound in X′. μ=0 forces I=O; off C the blowup is an isomorphism. Exact normal-graded and ideal-containment suppliers checked. Source Lemma 2.7.2 p.7 uses a characteristic-zero derivative shortcut; current proof is valid without it.

Accepted perfect-field closedness and replacement of circular invariant semicontinuity by a conditional finite-range assembly lemma. The derivative formula at p=k uses orders <k, whose factorials are invertible, and is valid at the stated endpoint. Finite boundary counts have finite-union closed superlevels. Noetherian descending closed order loci stabilize, yielding finitely many finite order values plus infinity. For lexicographic tuples the superlevel is {f>a}∪({f≥a}∩{g≥b}), closed with locally finite ranges; finite maxima preserve this. Branchwise invariant construction is expressly left for the proposition, rather than inferred from its definition. Source §3 p.16 and current derivative-support proof checked.

Accepted general-boundary/positive-mark reader qualification; amended the compressed smooth derivative argument by declaring the actual standard-smooth factorization supplier and spelling out the projection generator calculation. Base derivatives pull back; new-variable derivatives kill pulled-back generators, while Leibniz handles variable coefficients. The étale comparison then gives D^i equality for every smooth map, and products/powers/sums commute with ideal extension. Smooth order preservation keeps maximal order; E is auxiliary and causes no boundary restriction. μ=1 and empty fibres are included. Source Lemma 2.10.7 p.15; exact standard-smooth presentation and derivative/sum supplier statements read.

Accepted K-compatible coefficient-field, derivative-comparison, ideal-closure and inverse-preservation repairs; additionally corrected the Taylor calculation to include the multiplying T^i factor explicitly. A Taylor term of φ(f) alone lies in D^(i+s)(I)T^s, not T^(i+s); multiplying by φ(t) for t∈T^i gives the claimed summand of H. Cotangent linear algebra supplies A fixing the boundary subspace with (A-id)V⊂image(T) and A(u)=v; lifted increments in T give a continuous automorphism. Noetherian stabilization proves φ(T)=T. Closedness and Taylor expansion give both H containments, and identity modulo T fixes every support point and its residue ring. μ=1 and T containing boundary directions are allowed; no common complement for u,v is falsely assumed. Entire source Lemma 2.9.4 pp.10–11 and exact completion, coefficient-field, differential and graded suppliers checked.

Reader contract enrichment is sound; amended the ill-typed Statement I|U′ because U′ is an open in X′, not X. It now restricts I to U before transformation and restricts that transform to U′, as the proof already does. Derivative-transform inclusion puts u/y in T(I′). At its zeros on the exceptional divisor one chooses u as a center parameter and a distinct exceptional parameter, so u/y is an order-one chart coordinate. The u-index chart has no zeros (u/y is a unit); saturation gives the strict hypersurface everywhere. Empty center and an emptied hypersurface cause no stalk problem. Statement mathematics and global/local support scope are otherwise retained. Source Lemma 2.7.4/2.7.6 pp.7–8 and current exact transform interfaces checked.

Accepted safe-characteristic qualification of clause (4). Checked every algebraic clause: μ=1 gives H=I; every omitted term lies in T^μ, the last retained term. In D^(μ-1)(D^i I T^i), either the first derivative factor lies in T or the derivative budget leaves a tangent factor untouched, proving T(H)=T(I) both ways. Same-mark literal sums and iterated marked sums are equivalent under AC. For μ>1, D^μ I=O in the safe range makes D I maximal order; differentiating H puts all terms into H(D I,μ-1), with the top T^(μ-1) absorbed by the final term. Source Lemma 2.9.1 p.9 and exact derivative/sum interfaces checked.

Accepted general-boundary and μ≥1 reader corrections. Amended the inaccurate phrase that new-variable derivatives annihilate the whole extended ideal: they annihilate its pulled-back generators, and coefficient derivatives stay in the ideal by Leibniz. Declared the exact standard-smooth factorization supplier instead of relying on an order lemma for that assertion. Projection plus étale derivative equality proves smooth derivative equality; order preservation makes the pulled-back marking maximal, tangent ideals pull back, and the finite H sum then agrees termwise. Every characteristic and an arbitrary ordered SNC E are allowed because the equality uses only derivatives and ideal extension. Source Lemma 2.9.3 p.10 and exact local-presentation/differential suppliers checked.

Accepted the original-coefficient transform induction and safe-characteristic/boundary qualifications. Completed transverse expansion has coefficients ∂^αf/α! for |α|<μ, so initial restricted derivative order bounds give ambient order μ in both directions. Track J_(r,i), the actual transforms of original restricted derivatives with mark μ-r; coefficients transform by a^-(μ-|α|), preserving membership. Changing only tangent coefficient coordinates adapts smooth centers without recomputing C(I_i). This proves support equality at every stage; conversely the equality and omitted containing-boundary convention make each restricted center admissible in the ambient scheme. Disjoint centers induce isomorphisms. Factorials are invertible in the exact stated range, μ=1 is included, and empty restricted charts have no stalk. Full source Lemma 2.10.4 pp.14–15 checked, with its printed derivative-index shorthand interpreted by the chart calculation.

Accepted full exceptional-support induction. Read all six steps and source Lemma 2.9.5 pp.11–13. Two separate cotangent parameter systems with increments in T, together with common residue coordinates, give étale maps. Open diagonals isolate their equal scheme-theoretic pullbacks over S=V(T). At support points the completed comparison is the proved T-congruent automorphism; outside S, T and hence H are unit, so completed equality plus faithful flatness glues H ideals. Equality T(H)=T(I) initializes common tangent pullbacks. At each test blowup reduced centers contain T_i; equality modulo T_i gives identical inverse center ideals. Differences of ratio coordinates lie in e^-1T_i=T_(i+1), on common charts where both normalized denominators are units. Thus agreement persists on transformed support and controlled H transforms are equal; saturation preserves matching hypersurfaces. This is equality of homogenized transforms, not a fabricated equality of original nonhomogenized ideals. AC and characteristic zero are explicitly retained.

Accepted correction of (x²,y²)≠(x,y)² and full direct second obstruction. In characteristic 2 ordinary derivative iterates stay (x²,y²), whose nonzero origin germs have order at least 2, so there is no tangent section through the origin despite maximal order 2. For f=x²+yz³+zw³+y⁷w, substitution (t³²,t⁷,t¹⁹,t¹⁵) annihilates f and all first derivatives; polynomial degree in x bounds the order by 2. The four distinct weights 32,7,19,15 are each outside the additive semigroup of nonlinear combinations of those weights, so a nonzero linear part cannot vanish on the curve. This disproves a regular hypersurface containing the top locus without claiming equality with that locus or a blowup-persistence theorem. Read Hauser 2003 §14 Example 1 pp.387–388 from the complete downloaded PDF; web fetch timed out but the shell full-text retrieval succeeded. Both examples refute only the asserted mechanism, not positive-characteristic resolution.

Accepted perfection/p>μ inherited from coefficient restriction. At a contained center the exact previous coefficient-support theorem applies; a disjoint center is an isomorphism on a neighbourhood of S_i and leaves both restricted transforms and support unchanged. Induction on these two step types gives the asserted identity. Isomorphisms are valid test steps, and the extension convention now only inserts them. No assertion is made for centers partly intersecting S_i. Source Lemma 2.10.5 p.15 and current exact restriction/transform interfaces checked.

Confirmed refuter:26:1 against the exact post-reader carrier: u is defined only on U, so global supports on X_i cannot be compared with V(u)_i. The reported example I=m_(0,0)^2∩m_(1,0)^2 on A², μ=2, U omitting (1,0), u=x has a second global support point outside U already at stage 0. Explicit x∈support rules out a vacuous unit tangent and empty hypersurface in the proper-containment claim. At stage zero codimension ≥2 gives a nonempty hypersurface complement of the support; it survives every center because centers lie in support, proving strict containment at all stages. Current coefficient-restriction and tangent-persistence suppliers prove clauses (2)–(4) under AC and char0/perfect p>μ. Source Lemma 2.10.6 p.15 repeats the global shorthand, so its logical local proof, not its printed overstatement, is used. Reader correction from exact codimension 2 to ≥2 and perfection are retained. Direct consumer uses are local maximal-contact charts and require no mathematical narrowing.

Accepted the reader residual-order, rational encoding, boundary-count and finite monomial-tree repairs; additionally made the induction input and stratum components explicit and supplied ν=0,rho=empty on the infinity branches and inv=0 in the monomial branch. Smooth intersections may be disconnected, so resolve their irreducible components separately: contained components are blown up first, while each other restricted coefficient ideal is generically nonzero. This meets the lower-dimensional theorem rather than applying it to a zero restriction. Checked all nine steps against the entire source Proposition 3.0.8/§3 pp.16–21. Track only the boundary fixed at Step 1 start; each boundary pass drops its count, and lower-dimensional resolutions handle the proper restrictions. After codimension-one removal, local maximal-contact charts use the repaired local lemma, with gluing supplying invariant independence and matched centers. The companion is used only on its residual-max neighbourhood: transformed residual order ≤r and clearing companion support forces <r. r=0 is monomial. Inclusion-minimal threshold subsets give new exceptional exponent sum(A)-μ<a_j, so monomial order drops over each center; finite branching with the initial integer bound proves finite termination. Piecewise superlevels are closed on the closed leading-coordinate strata, including infinity branches; finite ranges and matched local charts give closed maximum centers. Étale comparison is pointwise and skips missing global maxima by isomorphism steps. AC/generic nonzero/μ≥1 and the dimension-zero case are retained. The localized refined-Giraud statement suffices for the actual affine-open uses.

Accepted correction of the ambient-prefix formula to (0,1,0,0), the rational encoding of each source pair (1,0). Clarified that the number of repeated pairs is the local codimension k at x, avoiding a constant-codimension assumption on disconnected smooth ambients. A lifted mark-one ideal contains the k immersion parameters; each is a tangent direction, and the support is the same embedded closed subscheme. Repeated coefficient/maximal-contact restriction prefixes the invariant, leaving ν and rho unchanged. The constant prefix makes maximum centers agree and blowups restrict to the corresponding blowups of X; k=0 gives no prefix. These are comparisons of the supplied canonical algorithm, with existence over nonclosed fields supplied by the later descent theorem. Read full source §4.2 p.24 and all exact current algorithm/tangent supplier statements.

Accepted the dimension-zero repair: generic nonvanishing gives unit ideals and empty support; a blowup of an entire zero-dimensional component cannot be excused as an isomorphism. Four-step proof checked: conjugation transports K-derivations under the semilinear ring isomorphism, and hence H/C; local-ring isomorphisms preserve orders, SNC strata and boundary labels. Induction transports lower-dimensional restrictions, companions, monomial thresholds and all canonical centers. Relabelling the K′-structure through σ permits the smooth-base-change interface; invariant comparison uses the underlying isomorphism, not K-linearity. Positive mark and generic nonzero on every component are retained; empty support gives identity. Full source Proposition 4.3.2 pp.24–25 checked.

Accepted pointwise residual-order versus global-maximum distinction; additionally repaired the same missing-maximum issue in the monomial endpoint and explicitly handled empty pullback support before taking maxima. When an étale image misses a residual-max pass, all inverse centers are empty; with matching maxima the companions pull back and the maximal-order comparison applies. In the monomial branch rho and ν are pointwise preserved: a missing global rho maximum gives an isomorphism, whereas a met maximum gives the canonical pulled-back center. Iterating yields precisely an extension, rather than incorrectly identifying an empty inverse center with a nonempty canonical one. Source Lemma 3.0.11 pp.21–22 and exact residual/étale/maximal-order interfaces checked.

Accepted local comparison of centers, removal of the undefined projection map, and general ordered-boundary qualification. Added the exact standard-smooth factorization supplier and explicit induction on the base dimension for the projection case: strata and chosen hypersurfaces are products, so lower-dimensional base resolutions commute by induction; H/C, residual orders and monomial thresholds pull back unchanged. Dimension zero has empty support by generic nonvanishing. Factor any smooth germ as étale after projection, apply the two comparisons and identify matching invariant maxima locally. A flat local map is faithfully flat, so nonzero ideal stalks remain nonzero and the pullback meets the existence hypotheses. Empty center steps are retained only as extensions. Full source §4.1 p.24 and exact current factorization, smooth-ideal and étale-pass interfaces checked.

Accepted finite-dimensional affine ideal descent replacing an unsupported general sheaf-descent claim, and the precise mark-one empty-boundary ambient interface. Added the descent of closed finite-range invariant superlevel strata, which uses the same stable-ideal argument. Independently read the full finite-dimensional Galois fixed-space proof: trace-dual finite sums span invariants with no infinite basis choice. Any f in an invariant ideal lies in V⊗L with V finite-dimensional and L finite Galois; embedding-extension supplies full Gal(L/K) stability, hence invariant vectors in A generate the ideal after scalar extension. Noetherian finite generation and localization glue unique center ideals; geometric-regularity descent makes the centers smooth. Flat blowup base change carries the exact Rees sequence, characteristic-zero derivative equality detects empty support, and smooth intersection/codimension descent gives SNC. μ≥1 and generic nonzero persist on geometric components; arbitrary Aut_K(Kbar) notation is not falsely called a finite Galois group. Source §4.4 p.25 and all exact Galois/flat/geometric-regularity interfaces checked.

Accepted replacement of a reduced SNC divisor assertion by an effective divisor with SNC support, allowing exceptional multiplicities (I=(x²) gives 2V(x)). Empty controlled support at mark 1 gives the unit ideal; unwinding each division gives precisely the product of exceptional factors. Properness uses blowup theorem clause 3, which has no global-generator requirement. Checked all four steps, including the finite intrinsic constant-field argument: Noether normalization bounds degrees of algebraic subfields, while clearing denominators and lying over contradict a transcendental element in any field subring. Therefore abstract ideal-preserving automorphisms act semilinearly on the componentwise intrinsic fields, and derivative equality over finite separable constants identifies the same algorithm; natural Rees lifts satisfy composition. Unit input gives the identity and empty divisor; generic nonzero excludes zero inputs on components. Source §§4.4–4.5 p.25 and exact normalization, maximal-ideal, finite-residue and lying-over supplier statements checked.

Accepted explicit AC inheritance, correct source locators and componentwise birationality for reduced Y. Independently read the complete source §4.7 Theorem 4.7.1 pp.25–26 and its codimension induction; its modified algorithm resolves exceptional residual factors first, then omits the blowup when a smooth transverse strict component becomes the next center. Thus it avoids the original smooth locus and handles components contained in the ambient by identity. Accepted the previously missing codimension induction and quotient-ideal lifting. Read every current step and complete source §4.7 pp.25–26. The special 3/2 monomial pass clears residual exceptional factors at mark 1. At the terminal source invariant, for c=1 the order-one isolated component has its exact ideal; for c>1 a tangent u∈J allows restriction to H and induction on c-1, and equality modulo (u) lifts because both J and I_Z contain u. Completed components are isolated and retained while the same bounded algorithm treats the remaining finite codimensions; remaining support away from them is principalized. The actual refined-Giraud use is on a local hypersurface and fits its repaired scope.

The common-ambient polynomial argument is sound. Full source Lemma 4.8.1/Proposition 4.8.2 pp.26–27 checked.

F1 now cites the actual embedded smooth-naturality theorem along with its marked-ideal underpinning. A function f lifts through the affine quotient to F, and ambient open restriction identifies the embedded resolutions. Empty overlap causes no condition. Full source Proposition 4.8.2 p.27 and the exact open/closed immersion and embedded compatibility interfaces checked.

subject: matrix-exponential-and-phi-function-actions
description: Refuter alleged that k=0 refutes the summary claim that every phi action is obtained from an augmented exponential.
resolution: False positive after independent current page, series definition, augmented theorem and Arnoldi algorithm review. For k>=1 the theorem gives phi_k(X)w as the top n coordinates of exp(B_k(X,w))(0,e_k). For k=0 let C=diag(X,0)=B_1(X,0). Its powers have top-left block X^j (including C^0), hence the absolutely convergent series gives exp(C)=diag(exp(X),1), and the top n entries of exp(C)(w,0) equal exp(X)w=phi_0(X)w. This also holds for X=0 and for n=0. Alternatively recurrence gives phi_0(X)w=w+phi_1(X)(Xw), obtainable from the theorem with B_1(X,Xw). No B_0 is needed. Thus the page claim that each phi action can be obtained from one augmented exponential is sound; the algorithm is free to evaluate k=0 directly. No page edit is warranted.
